title: Plan-Execution Errata: Frozen Batch B/C and Post-Freeze Canonical Lineage

errata_revisions.scope_snapshot: Recorded the first 23 Batch B/C admissions and the then-pending Batch D dependency transformation.

errata_revisions.reason: PR #5462 was correct for its 2026-08-30T20:45:00Z cutoff, but later governed events made its completion claim incomplete: all nine Batch C rows were subsequently superseded by V2 replacements, Training V2 and bridge-allowlist V3 required evidence-contract replacements, Batch D materialized against transformed dependencies, two post-freeze product gaps were discovered, and the exact deployment/write-proof outcomes were not recorded.

purpose: The frozen EXECUTION_TASK_CATALOG_2026-08-30.json (immutable planning evidence, 30 tasks) is never edited in place. This ledger records what the live supervisor actually did when it dispatched the 23 Batch B + Batch C child tasks from that catalog: canonical task rows cannot be amended in place, so any task that failed to materialize correctly under its catalog task_id was retired via `supersede` and re-created under a new one-to-one replacement id, never rewritten. This is a machine-checkable correction of the plan-vs-execution divergence; it does not change the frozen catalog's 30 task specs.

root_cause.summary: Batch A bootstrap (OPGAP-DEVTOOL-TARGET-REPO-BRIDGE-20260830) delivered a dev-bridge dispatcher that could route signed DevTaskPackets, but its allowlist of writable repositories was not derived from the live supervisor's coordination.repositories configuration. Batch B was materialized while only pantheon was configured; when Batch C's mixed pantheon/execute-plans packet drained, the dispatcher rejected it because execute-plans was not yet a configured repository.
root_cause.canonical_task_definitions_cannot_be_ame: ai_status.py has no update-in-place path for a task's id, artifacts, owner/reviewer pairing, or dependency binding once the row exists; the only lifecycle exits from a stuck todo/in_progress row are done, blocked, or supersede. Because the Batch B rows were created before the allowlist/command-runtime fixes existed, they could not be repaired by editing their depends_on or artifacts -- they had to be superseded by a new row that carries the corrected dependency binding.
root_cause.supervisor_gap_still_open: OPGAP-DEVTOOL-BRIDGE-REPO-ALLOWLIST-V3-20260830 (status: blocked as of this V2 snapshot) tracked the then-unresolved defect: the live supervisor still could not derive PANTHEON_ASSISTANT_DEV_BRIDGE_ALLOWED_REPOS from coordination.repositories on its own and depended on an operator-injected environment override. This is retained as historical V2 truth, not current status.
root_cause.post_freeze_resolution: The functional implementation was validated in PR #5459, then V3 was superseded only after OPGAP-DEVTOOL-BRIDGE-REPO-ALLOWLIST-V4-20260830 supplied the missing immutable evidence-manifest contract. V4 exact head f0e1481a1b07c95ec0800a9f93ac99da2ccbe46b merged as 5b0d02196acfc9c3ef956ae4c47865601bc43da6 via PR #5473. Repository allowlist derivation is therefore delivered; any frontend packet still requires a promoted command runtime containing that merge and remains fail-closed if the live registry omits execute-plans.

superseded_terminal_facts_do_not_satisfy: A task row whose terminal_outcome is 'superseded' is archived with terminal_status 'done' for bookkeeping, but the supervisor's dependency-satisfaction check binds to the specific task id named in depends_on. Every live Batch B/C/D row in ai-status.json now names the *-V2-20260830 (or original, for never-superseded Batch C) id explicitly; none depend on a superseded id. This ledger exists so that a reviewer diffing the frozen catalog's depends_on entries against live canonical state does not mistake the intentional supersede-then-rebind pattern for drift.

batch_d_dependency_transformation.description: OPGAP-BFF-MAIN-ASSEMBLY-20260830 (Batch D) is frozen in the catalog with depends_on naming the 14 Batch B ids plus the 5 Batch C support-router ids by their original catalog names. 14 of those names are now terminal-superseded and cannot satisfy a live dependency check; at materialization time Batch D's depends_on must be rebound to the 14 V2 replacement ids while the 5 unchanged Batch C support ids pass through unmodified. This is not yet materialized (Batch D is still gated on Batch B/C completion) -- this table documents the required rebinding so a future dispatch does not accidentally bind the frozen, terminal ids.
